paper_metadata.title: Investigation on high-temperature mechanical properties of Al–7Si–0.6Mg alloy by wire + arc additive manufacturing

evidence.quote: Al–7Si–0.6Mg alloy is widely used in aerospace indus- try because of its excellent specific strength, castabil- ity and corrosion resistance [1–4].
Specification and Model of Metal Wire: φ1.2mm ER4220 (Q/FSDG002-2018), produced by North East
WAAM Al–7Si–0.6Mg alloy, which was perpendicular to the rolling direction for the sub- strate, was prepared by single-layer and double-channel stacking forming method
T6 heat treatment was carried out on the formed sample in solid solution furnace and aging furnace with accuracy of ±3°C.

WAAM Al–7Si–0.6Mg alloy, which was perpendicular to the rolling direction for the sub- strate, was prepared by single-layer and double-channel stacking forming method, and control the interpass temperature between 160 and 180°C.
the solution treatment technology is 540°C×12h, the ramp rate is 7°Cmin–1
the quench medium is water (40°C) with quenching time 15min
the aging treatment technology is 175°C×4h

The specimens were heated to the required temper- ature with the furnace and kept for 30 min. Tensile tests were carried out with an electro-hydraulic servo tester (Instron 8872). The strains of high-temperature specimens were measured by axial furnace extensometer (3448-050M-020), and the strain rate during the tension testing was 0.0042 min–1.

When the temperature is lower than the aging temperature (RT, 100°C, 150°C), the main softening mechanism of the alloy is the coarsening of precipitates, but the coarsening rate is lower, as shown in Figure6(a–c), so the strength of the alloy decreases slowly.

When the temperature is higher than aging temperature (200°C,250°C), the alloy is exposed for 30min before stretching, showing a short over aging and the coarsening rate of precipitated phase increases, as shown in Figure6(d,e), accompanied by the transformation of β′′-phase to β′-phase or β-phase [30], which accelerates the strength decline of the alloy.

On the other hand, with the increase of temperature, the ability of atom diffusion and interface sliding are enhanced, and the ability of impeding dislocation is reduced, which also makes the mechanical properties of the alloy decline.
